title: The Indian man who was legally dead for nineteen years
hook: A man in India was legally dead for nineteen years while very much alive.
summary: Lal Bihari of Uttar Pradesh was declared dead on paper in 1975 so relatives could take his land, and spent until 1994 proving he was alive.
sources: Wikipedia: Lal Bihari - declared dead in 1975 in Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh; recognised as alive in 1994; added 'Mritak' to his name; founded Uttar Pradesh Mritak Sangh.
BBC News and The Guardian reports on Lal Bihari Mritak: relatives bribed officials to record him dead for land; he contested elections including against Rajiv Gandhi in 1989.

lines.text: A man in India was legally dead for nineteen years.
lines.caps: A *man in India | was legally *dead | for *nineteen years

lines.text: In nineteen seventy-six, Lal Bihari asked a bank for a loan.
lines.caps: In *1976, | Lal *Bihari | asked a *bank | for a *loan

lines.text: Officials checked their records and said he had died the year before.
lines.caps: Officials *checked | their *records | and said he had *died

lines.text: His relatives had bribed clerks, so they could take his land.
lines.caps: His *relatives | had *bribed clerks, | to take his *land

lines.text: To prove he lived, he stood against Rajiv Gandhi in an election.
lines.caps: To prove he *lived, | he stood *against | *Rajiv Gandhi

lines.text: He even added mritak, meaning dead, to his own name.
Only in nineteen ninety-four did the state record him as alive.
lines.caps: Only in *1994 | the state *recorded | him as *alive

lines.text: He had to fight for proof that he existed.
lines.caps: He had to *fight | for *proof | that he *existed

post.caption:
He was alive, but the paperwork said otherwise for nineteen years.
Would you have kept fighting this long?
